li_caption:
January 15, 2027 is the last estimated tax payment for 2026. A short check now beats a penalty in April.

What we look at before that date:

1. Do you need to pay? Generally yes if you expect to owe $1,000 or more for 2026 after withholding and refundable credits. Freelancers, 1099 workers and owners with profit and no withholding usually do.
2. The safe amount. Paying at least 90% of your 2026 tax or 100% of your 2025 tax, whichever is less, avoids the underpayment penalty.
3. Higher income last year. If your 2025 AGI was over $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately), the prior-year test is 110%, not 100%.
4. The file-early option. If you file your 2026 return by February 1, 2027 and pay the full balance, you don't need the January 15 payment.

NJ and NY have their own estimated payments due January 15 as well, and rules vary by state.
